blocks.text: How to use medical coding software help on your Mac

Your day as a medical coder involves constant switching between different windows. You might have an EHR like Epic or a native Mac application like MacPractice open in one space. At the same time, you are likely checking coding manuals or web-based portals like AAPC Codify. This context switching kills your momentum. Lazur stays in the notch of your Mac. You hold the Option and Command keys to ask a question about what is on your screen. If you cannot find a specific setting in your billing software, ask Lazur where it is. Lazur will draw a circle around the menu item. This prevents you from clicking through submenus when you are in a rush to finish a batch of claims.
Managing the administrative burden of coding

Administrative burden is the biggest hurdle in your daily workflow. You have to verify insurance information, manage queries from clinical staff, and address denials. These tasks often require typing long, repetitive explanations. Instead of typing these manually, use the dictation capability. Hold the fn key to dictate your notes or email responses. Lazur formats the text for you. You can build your own snippets for common coding errors or documentation requests. This keeps your communication professional and consistent. Remember that you are responsible for the accuracy of the text you generate. Always review your output before sending it to a physician or a billing department.

When you need to cross-reference a procedure code, you do not want to leave your main window. Use the research capability to ask Lazur to look up a specific guideline while you stay focused on your primary task. Lazur uses its own Chrome tabs to find the information. It then summarizes the findings for you. This is useful when you are verifying CPT or HCPCS codes. You can stay in your EHR and listen to the summary without losing your place. This reduces the number of times you have to click away from your active record.

blocks.text: Best practices for Mac medical coders

Keep your workspace clean. If you use multiple monitors, keep your EHR on the main display. Put your coding reference tools on the secondary screen. Use the macOS Mission Control feature to organize your spaces. Assign your coding software to a specific desktop. This allows you to swipe between your email, your EHR, and your research browser. When you need help, ask Lazur to point at the specific button you need to select. If you are struggling with a complex menu in Microsoft 365 or a web portal, Lazur can guide you through the process one click at a time.

Always check your employer's policy regarding the use of voice assistants and AI tools. Never dictate or process sensitive patient health information (PHI) in a way that violates your facility's security protocols.
blocks.title: Data Privacy Reminder

faq.question: Can Lazur access my patient records directly?
faq.answer: No. Lazur does not have direct access to your EHR database. It only sees the screen content you show it while you hold the activation keys.

faq.question: Is my voice data stored?
faq.answer: No. Audio and screenshots are sent to the AI service only to provide an answer to your request. They are not stored or used to train models.

faq.question: Does Lazur work with all coding software?
faq.answer: Lazur works on any macOS application. It does not integrate with specific software, so it works as a visual and voice assistant for any interface you have on your screen.
